title: Why Are Groceries So Expensive? (Up 32% Since 2020)
description:
U.S. grocery prices (CPI food at home) are up 32.5% since January 2020, and this year's classic Thanksgiving dinner for 10 costs $58.63, more than 6% above last year, with the 16-lb turkey up 10%, per the American Farm Bureau. Coffee is up 122% ($4.17 to $9.25 a pound), ground beef 74%, eggs 59% after peaking at $6.23 a dozen. We look at why food costs more (fuel, labor, packaging: under 6 cents of each grocery dollar reaches the farm), groceries vs your other bills, and whether pay kept up (average hourly pay +33.7%).
